screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study evaluating intracervical nitroprusside gel versus placebo immediately prior to IUD placement in nulliparous women, with subject-reported pain with IUD insertion as the primary outcome. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating oral ibuprofen 800 mg versus placebo 30–45 min prior to IUD insertion, with pain measured by VAS immediately following insertion. Clear RCT of a pharmacological pain intervention.

Randomised trial comparing delayed bladder emptying (full bladder) versus immediate emptying before IUC insertion. Pain scores were measured and reported as a secondary outcome. Included conservatively as it evaluates an insertion intervention with pain as an assessed outcome.

Randomized, open, parallel-group trial comparing 2% lidocaine intracervical injection versus oral ibuprofen 400 mg for LNG-IUS insertion pain in women without previous vaginal delivery. Pain evaluated immediately and up to 6 hours post-insertion. Meets inclusion criteria.

Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT evaluating oral ibuprofen 800 mg versus placebo 45 min prior to LNG-IUS insertion, with pain scores at tenaculum placement and insertion. Aligns with review selection criteria.

Double-blind, multicenter RCT evaluating vaginal misoprostol 400 μg versus placebo 3 h prior to IUD insertion. Pain during insertion was measured as a secondary outcome. Misoprostol is a cervical ripening agent listed in the review background.

RCT evaluating buccal misoprostol 400 mcg versus placebo 90 min prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women. Patient-reported pain at multiple time points (including insertion and 5 min post-insertion) was measured by VAS. Meets inclusion criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating sublingual misoprostol 400 mcg versus placebo 3 h prior to consecutive LNG-IUS replacement. Pain at insertion was assessed (reported as no/mild pain). Included as an RCT of a recognized intervention with pain measured.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating oral ibuprofen 400 mg versus placebo at least 45 min before copper IUD insertion, with pain measured by VAS immediately after insertion. Clear inclusion.

Single-blind randomized controlled trial evaluating sublingual misoprostol plus diclofenac versus diclofenac alone one hour before IUD insertion in parous women with only elective CS. The study objective explicitly includes reducing pain, and insertion-related outcomes were assessed. Included conservatively.

Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluating ibuprofen 600 mg versus placebo in connection with IUD insertion, with pain assessed by Numerical Rating Scales during insertion and up to three days post-insertion. Meets all criteria.

Randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing oral tramadol 50 mg, naproxen sodium 550 mg, and placebo 1 hour before IUD insertion, with pain intensity evaluated by VAS during insertion. Evaluates active analgesic interventions for insertion pain.

Double-blind, randomized, controlled trial evaluating buccal misoprostol 400 mcg versus placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women. Patient-reported pain immediately prior to and after IUD insertion was measured by VAS. Meets inclusion criteria.

Randomized, double-blind clinical trial evaluating intracervical 2% lidocaine gel versus placebo prior to uterine sounding and IUD insertion, with pain rated by VAS at multiple time points. Clear RCT of a local anesthetic intervention.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study evaluating vaginal 0.5-mg nitroglycerin gel versus placebo 30 min prior to IUD placement in nulliparous women. Primary outcome was subject-reported pain with passage of the IUD through the cervix. Meets criteria.

Randomized trial evaluating a 1% lidocaine paracervical block versus no local anesthetic before IUD insertion. Women marked pain on a 100-mm VAS at several procedural points including IUD insertion. Meets inclusion criteria.

Randomized double-blind controlled trial with three arms (lidocaine 2% gel, lubricant gel, no intervention) for copper IUD insertion. Pain during insertion was measured by 0–10 cm VAS immediately after insertion. Clear inclusion.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study evaluating intrauterine infusion of 2% lidocaine versus normal saline 3 min prior to IUD insertion. Pain scores during IUD insertion were measured on a 0–9-point scale. Meets criteria.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating sublingual misoprostol 400 μg plus diclofenac versus diclofenac alone 1 h prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women. Pain was estimated on a VAS at insertion. Meets inclusion criteria.

Randomized, double-blind clinical trial evaluating vaginal misoprostol 400 μg versus placebo 4 h prior to IUD insertion in nulligravidas. Moderate-to-severe pain at insertion was a key reported outcome, with significant reduction in the misoprostol group. Clear inclusion.

RCT using randomized blocks evaluating inhaled lavender scent versus placebo 30 min before IUD insertion. Pain caused by IUD insertion was measured immediately after insertion by VAS (0–10). Although a complementary therapy, it is an RCT evaluating an intervention for insertion-related pain.

Randomized controlled trial evaluating self-administered misoprostol 400 μg versus placebo 3–4 h before IUD insertion in nulliparous women. Patient-perceived pain during insertion was measured by validated VAS. Meets inclusion criteria.

Randomized controlled trial (phase-II) evaluating a novel topical lidocaine formulation (SHACT) versus placebo at IUD insertion. Mean VAS pain scores during and after insertion were primary efficacy outcomes. Clear inclusion.

Prospective, single-blinded, controlled study of paracervical block versus placebo versus no treatment. The abstract does not describe randomization; it is not clearly an RCT. Because the review selection criteria explicitly require RCTs, this study is excluded.

Registered randomized clinical trial evaluating misoprostol 400 mcg versus placebo prior to IUD insertion in nulliparous women. The primary outcome was pain at insertion measured by 100-mm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating self-administered vaginal lidocaine gel versus placebo for reducing pain during IUD insertion; reports self-reported pain on a VAS at insertion and tenaculum placement.
Descriptive clinical article presenting a personal technique for intracervical anesthesia; no control group, no randomization, not an RCT.
Prospective cohort study comparing pain by obstetric history; no intervention randomized, not an RCT.
Qualitative interview study exploring perceptions of IUD non-users; not an RCT and does not evaluate a pain intervention.
Consensus review article offering practical non-pharmacological advice; not a primary RCT.
GRADE methodology article unrelated to IUD insertion pain interventions.
Committee opinion/guideline on adolescent LARC; not an RCT evaluating a pain intervention.
Narrative review summarizing pain management evidence; not a primary RCT.
Narrative review of misoprostol uses in gynecology; not an RCT focused on IUD insertion pain.
Single-group observational study of actual versus expected pain with a modified insertion technique; no randomization or control group.
GRADE methodology article unrelated to IUD insertion pain interventions.
Explicitly labeled as a nonrandomized prospective study predicting difficult insertion; not an RCT evaluating a pain intervention.
Commentary/review noting lack of guidelines; not an RCT.
Systematic review of intrauterine anesthesia across gynecologic procedures; not a primary RCT.
Observational questionnaire study of self-selected oral analgesia use before IUD fitting; no randomization or control group.
Technical report on adolescent contraception; not an RCT evaluating IUD insertion pain.
Meta-analysis of RCTs on analgesics for IUD placement; not a primary RCT.
RCT evaluating nitric oxide donors for cervical ripening before surgical abortion; wrong population and procedure, not IUD insertion.
Cross-sectional survey of doctor practices; not an RCT.
Methodology paper describing a prospective meta-analysis collaboration; no patient-level pain outcomes reported.
Narrative review/commentary on misoprostol for IUD insertion; not a primary RCT.

RCT evaluating meptazinol for treatment of pain days after IUD insertion rather than prevention of insertion-related pain; does not report self-reported pain scores at tenaculum placement, during insertion, or within six hours after insertion.
Randomized clinical trial comparing lavender aromatherapy versus placebo and control for pain during IUD insertion; reports self-reported pain scores on a VAS.
Descriptive article presenting a simplified paracervical block technique without randomization or control group.
Cochrane review of NSAIDs for IUD-related bleeding and pain; not a primary RCT.
